summary: Jason M. Wirth works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki (attested 2017–2019) and became a professor of philosophy at Seattle University around 2004.

Jason McCombs specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a B.S. at the University of Michigan and completed his PhD at UCLA by 2014 under Gregory Schopen, later serving as a lecturer at UCLA.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a master's at UT Austin and a PhD in 2001 at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon, later becoming Associate Professor and Chair at Wilfrid Laurier University.

Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick (attested 2015–2016) and held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.

Jay Jasanoff is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his bachelor's at Harvard (~1959–1963). He taught at UC Berkeley, Harvard (1970–1978; 1998 as Diebold Professor), and Cornell University (~1978–1998 as full professor).

Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied with teachers including Robert A. F. Thurman and Ngawang Samten. His appointments include Hampshire College (1980–1995), Smith College (~1999 onward), Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Melbourne.

Jay M. Bernstein is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1971–1975). He held academic posts at the University of Essex (~1978–1997), Vanderbilt University (~1997–2001), and The New School (~2001).

Jay Valentine specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware (1992), Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, where he earned his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer.
Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar was a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna from circa 1935 to 1938.

Jayandra Soni is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University (~1975–1978) and McMaster University (~1982–1987). He lectured at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and became Generalsekretär of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (2012).

Jayashree Sathe is an Indologist and linguist. She has held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, serving as editor in chief (attested 2011) and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

Jaś Elsner works in archaeology and religious studies, earning a BA and PhD at King's College, Cambridge. He held positions at the Courtauld Institute, Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1999), and Oxford University as Professor of Late Antique Art (2014).
Jean Dantinne was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Étienne Lamotte and held a position as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian. He taught at Suryavarman II School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras, was a researcher and associate member at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, and was an associate member at the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He founded and directed the French Institute of Pondicherry (1955–1977), directed the EFEO (1956–1977), and held chairs at EPHE (1941–1978) and the Collège de France (1951–1978).

Jean Kellens is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and Indological studies. He studied at the University of Liège and University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding posts at Mainz (~1974–1982), Liège (~1982–1993), and the Collège de France (1993).

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Amsterdam. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and served as Professor at Leiden University and Director of the Kern Institute.

Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held professorships at INALCO (1923–1930), EPHE (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean Rouch studied at École des Ponts ParisTech, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and the Institut d'ethnologie under Marcel Mauss (~1939–1941). He held an academic post at Paris Nanterre University.

Jean-Baptiste Biot was a scholar active in archaeology, Sinology, and other fields who studied at the École Polytechnique. He served as professor at the École Centrale de Beauvais (1797) and Collège de France (1800–1862), and taught at the Science Faculty of Paris.
